references.text: God creates the great sea creatures and every living thing that swarms in the water, as well as all kinds of birds – the direct fulfillment of God's word in verse 20.
God blesses the newly created water creatures and birds and commands them to be fruitful and multiply.
God creates land animals with a similar creative command, expanding the work of creation to include all living things on the earth.
God forms every beast of the field and every bird under heaven, a parallel account of the creation of living beings.
The psalmist praises God's many works of creation, including the sea that swarms with life – a hymn of praise reflecting the creation of water-dwelling creatures.
Calls on all creatures, including sea animals and birds, to praise the Lord as their Creator.
David's psalm about humanity's dominion over creation, including birds under heaven and fish in the sea.
Believers confess in prayer that God is the Creator of heaven, earth, the sea, and everything in them, in line with the creation account.
1:20 shows how the creation of birds unfolds within the framework of the expanse created in 1:6.
The creation of birds and fish in 1:20 establishes the creatures over which humanity is given authority in 1:26.
1:28 confirms humanity's dominion over the creatures (birds/fish) that were created in 1:20.
The creation of the contents of the sea in 1:20 is the foundation for the song of praise in Psalm 96:11.
God's command to Noah in 8:17 restores the creative word about swarming and fruitfulness from 1:20.
The song of praise in 1 Chronicles 16:32 celebrates the contents of the sea that were created in 1:20.
Contrast between the creation of life in 1:20 and the call to death in Ezekiel 39:17.
The separation of the waters in 1:7 establishes the space (the firmament) in which the birds fly in 1:20.
The song of praise in Psalm 98:7 celebrates the contents of the sea that were created in 1:20.
1:30 provides food for the creatures (birds/animals) that were created in 1:20.
Psalm 148:4 calls the waters above the firmament to praise, which refers directly to the creation structure in 1:6-7 and 1:20.
Revelation 14:7 calls for worship of the Creator of the sea and its contents that were created in 1:20.
